aviso: This text explains in plain language how MuseLearn works. If your school has its own rules about student data, they also apply.

privacidad.intro: MuseLearn is a study platform for secondary school teachers and students. This policy explains what data we use, what for, who we share it with and what your rights are. It is governed by Dominican Republic Law 172-13 on personal data protection.

parrafos: MuseLearn is an educational project developed by José Enrique Ulloa, a Technology teacher in the Dominican Republic. When a school uses MuseLearn with its students, the school and its teachers decide which classes and tasks are created; MuseLearn stores and processes that data to provide the service.
Account data: name, email, role (teacher or student), language and appearance and study-hours preferences.
Schoolwork: classes, tasks, submissions (text, files and notebook photos), tutor conversations, comprehension-check answers, comprehension reports, practice routes and teacher comments.
Voice: when you answer by voice, the audio is sent to be turned into text and is not stored. We only keep the text of your answer.
Minimal technical data needed for the app to work securely (for example, your session and error logs without the content of your tasks).
To organize your study week, give you tutor help without solving your task, check that you understood what you handed in, and show your teacher your progress.
We don't sell your data, we don't show ads and we don't use it to build commercial profiles.
MuseLearn uses Meta models (Muse) to analyze tasks, chat as a tutor, ask comprehension questions and write reports. Only what each feature needs is sent.
We don't use Meta's “Contributor” tier, where data may be used to train models. Review suggestions for teachers use only aggregated data, without student names.
AI can make mistakes. Grades and decisions about students are always made by the teacher.
With your teacher and your class, according to your role: each student sees only their own work; each teacher sees only their classes.
With the providers that run the service: Supabase (database and files), Vercel (app hosting), Meta (AI models) and Google, only if you or your teacher connect a Google or Google Classroom account.
With authorities, only if the law requires it.

MuseLearn is designed for secondary school students and is used through their school and teacher. If you are under 18, use MuseLearn with permission from your parent or guardian, or from your school according to its rules.
If you are a parent or guardian and want to review or delete your child's data, write to the contact email.
As long as your account exists. If you delete your account, your data and files are deleted. If a teacher deletes a class or a task, whatever depends on it is deleted.
Voice audio is not stored: it is transcribed and discarded.
You can access your data, correct it, ask for it to be deleted and object to its use.
In Settings → Privacy and data you can download your data and delete your account. You change your name and language in My profile. For anything else, write to us.

Connections are encrypted and the database enforces per-user access rules: nobody can see another student's work or another teacher's classes. No system is perfect: if we detect a problem affecting your data, we will let you know.
If we change this policy, we will update the version date and ask you to accept it again when you sign in.

terminos.intro: By creating an account or using MuseLearn you accept these terms. Take your time: they are short.

parrafos: A study companion that organizes your week, helps you with questions and hints without doing your homework, and checks that you understood what you handed in. For teachers, it is a tool to assign tasks and see their class's comprehension.
Use your real name and your own email. One account per person. Keep your password safe and don't share it.
Choose the right role: teacher or student. Teacher accounts are for real teachers.
MuseLearn exists for learning. Don't try to get answers from the tutor, don't hand in someone else's work as yours, and answer the comprehension check yourself.
Don't upload offensive or violent content, content that isn't yours, or other people's personal data that the task doesn't need.
Don't try to access other people's accounts or data or disrupt the app.
Use MuseLearn with your students according to your school's rules, including family consent when needed.
Review the AI's suggestions (tasks, reviews and comments) before using them. Assessment and grades are your decision.
What you write and upload is still yours. You give us permission to store and process it only to provide the service, as the Privacy policy explains.
The AI's answers, questions and reports may contain errors. Use them as support, not as absolute truth. If something seems wrong or inappropriate, tell your teacher.
MuseLearn is under active development. We do our best for it to work well, but it may have failures, changes or pauses. There are daily AI usage limits so the service is enough for everyone.
You can delete your account at any time from Settings. We may suspend an account that breaks these terms or puts other users at risk.
MuseLearn is provided as is. To the extent the law allows, we are not responsible for losses caused by service failures or by the use of the AI's suggestions.
These terms are governed by the laws of the Dominican Republic. If we change them, we will update the version date and ask you to accept them again.

comoFunciona.intro: Handing in homework does not prove learning. MuseLearn connects study planning, guided help and the student’s explanation with what their teacher sees.
comoFunciona.capturas: Demo screenshots use fictional data. The pictured screens are in Spanish; AI responses in this demo are simulated.
secciones: Each task is analyzed for difficulty, time and concepts. Today and Week fit the work around your schedule; notices explain changes to the plan.
Today study plan with blocks and priorities
A tutor that does not do the homework
The tutor guides with questions and hints. The teacher chooses the help level: hints, similar examples or a concept explanation.
Socratic tutor asking a guiding question
After submitting text, files or a notebook photo, explain your own work by voice or text. Receive a report by concept and a practice route. You can also provide evidence for a Classroom task.
Comprehension check asking about submitted work

The dashboard compares who submitted with who demonstrated understanding, with evidence by concept. Teachers can comment, optionally grade, return work for correction and export CSV. AI can make mistakes; the teacher makes the final assessment.
Teacher comprehension dashboard with fictional data
AI proposes a task from a topic. It also suggests review activities using aggregated data without names and drafts feedback. The teacher reviews and edits before saving.
Creating a task from an AI proposal
trabajos: Socratic tutor, comprehension questions, reading notebook photos, report and route
Batch task analysis and weekly planning
comoFunciona.privacidadTexto: Students access their own work and teachers their own classes. Audio is transcribed and not stored. You can download your data and delete your account. We do not use the Contributor tier with student data.
